title: Postdoctoral Fellowship in Philosophy, Politics and Economics University of Pennsylvania
description:
Postdoctoral Fellowship in Philosophy, Politics and Economics
University of Pennsylvania


Location: PPE Program, University of Pennylvania
(Philadelphia, PA)
Open Date: Sep 22, 2026
Deadline:

The Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) Program at the
University of Pennsylvania invites applications for a postdoctoral
fellowship beginning Fall 2027 (appointment start date July 1,
2027). The fellowship lasts one year, with the possibility of
annual renewal for up to four additional years, contingent upon a
satisfactory performance review and funding.

This position is designed to support a talented economist working
in behavioral or experimental economics, or a related PPE area.
Duties include pursuing an independent research agenda and teaching
three (3) courses each academic year, consisting of two (2)
advanced interdisciplinary seminars and one (1) research seminar
focused on training a small cohort of students in field-specific
research methods. Seminar topics will be developed in consultation
with the program and should reflect the fellow's expertise while
engaging substantively with PPE.



Qualifications
Applicants must have completed a PhD in Economics or a closely
related field by the start of the appointment, along with a
demonstrated record of interdisciplinary engagement, a strong
research trajectory, and prior teaching experience.



Application Instructions
Application Materials


Cover letter describing research interests, current projects,
and fit with the PPE Program
Curriculum vitae
Teaching dossier
Two course descriptions for upper level undergraduate seminars
(approx 150 words each)
Two letters of recommendation



Interviews are anticipated to take place in December and January.
For questions, please contact ppe-program@sas.upenn.edu.



To apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/194199


Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

The University of Pennsylvania is an equal opportunity employer.
Candidates are considered for employment without regard to race,
color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, creed, national origin
(including shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics), citizenship
status, age, disability, veteran status or any class protected
under applicable federal, state, or local law.
